E2 mentions thermal analysis for phase transitions but provides no data on segregation or surface-initiated melting. premises: Differences in surface free energy among Fe, Ni, Cr, Co, Cu drive selective atomic migration to nanoparticle surfaces.
This segregation enriches lower-melting elements at surfaces, locally reducing the melting temperature.
Premelting initiates at these surface sites as localized melt domains.
These premelt regions coalesce to form a fully melted state at a temperature lower than bulk predictions.
This mechanism is dominant only for nanoparticles below ~20 nm under heating that restricts complete bulk diffusion.
